newsitem.title: CANADA: A Wayne Gretzky Street? 'No way' Say Hometown Callers.
newsitem.headline: A Wayne Gretzky Street? 'No way' Say Hometown Callers.

text.p: Residents of Wayne Gretzky's hometown are giving the cold shoulder towards a proposal to name a street after the hockey superstar.
Callers to a local Brantford, Ontario newspaper's talk-back line overwhelmingly voiced disapproval against the idea this week.
Gretzky, the National Hockey League's all-time scoring leader who will play for the New York Rangers this season, was born and raised in Brantford, an hour's drive from Toronto.
Ron Kowalsky, managing editor of the paper that ran the talk-back line, said Thursday, "I assumed people would have been overwhelmingly in favor."
Instead, callers left messages like, "What has Gretzky done for the city lately?" and "Enough is enough."
A city counsellor proposed changing a road to the Wayne Gretzky Parkway. The plan was still at the street naming committee level.
"It's a Canadian thing. If you get too big here, people want to pull you back to reality again," said Kowalsky.
